transcript.content: Hello. I'm glad you're here today. What brings you in to see me?
Thanks for seeing me. I’ve developed this intense, irrational fear of going into the ocean, even though I grew up surfing.
Did this fear start after a specific frightening or traumatic event in the ocean, or did it seem to develop out of nowhere?

It definitely started after a specific event about eleven months ago. I was out for an early-morning surf and got caught in a sudden rip current that pulled me far out from the shore. It completely shook me up, and a lifeguard had to come out and rescue me.
Since that scary event, do you find yourself having unwanted memories, flashbacks, or nightmares about being pulled out by the current?

No, I don't really have nightmares or sudden flashbacks out of nowhere. My mind only jumps back to that scary moment when I'm actually looking at the ocean or picturing myself trying to paddle back out.
Since that incident, have you felt generally more on edge, easily startled, or had trouble sleeping, even when you aren't near or thinking about the ocean?

No, I haven't really had any trouble sleeping or felt easily startled when I'm away from the water. All of my anxiety and those physical reactions are strictly tied to being near the ocean, the beach, or even just thinking about getting back in.

latest_inference.note: Previously, the candidates were F40.2 and F43.1. The patient denies generalized hyperarousal, insomnia, or spontaneous intrusive flashbacks/nightmares, which makes PTSD (F43.1) highly unlikely. Their symptoms are strictly bound to the ocean, beach, or thoughts of the ocean, which is characteristic of a Specific Phobia (F40.2) initiated by a traumatic event. Therefore, F43.1 is ruled out, leaving F40.2 as the sole candidate.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits an intense, irrational fear of the ocean (F40.2) that developed after a frightening rip current incident 11 months ago. The anxiety and physiological reactivity are strictly bound to the ocean, beach, or thoughts of entering the water, and are not present generally. Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (F43.1) was considered but ruled out because the patient does not experience spontaneous intrusive symptoms (flashbacks, nightmares) or generalized hyperarousal/sleep disturbance when away from the phobic stimulus.
